findings.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The `if (immediateDelete) { await client.request(...); return; }` branch leaves the reminder row `scheduled` and `cancelled` unchanged while the non-immediate branch marks it cancelled and the SMS manager deletes rows, creating channel-specific terminal states and stale email records that downstream reconciliation cannot interpret consistently.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — The `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel) { await client.request(...); ... workflowReminderToDelete = prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...) }` loop performs one serial SendGrid call and one delete per cancelled reminder across all users, so a backlog grows as N external round trips and any mid-loop failure leaves a partially reconciled, repeatedly scanned set instead of an idempotent claimed batch.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:574 — The `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...) ... })` fire-and-forget transition is not awaited before the mutation creates replacement reminders, allowing old cancellation and new scheduling to interleave and leaving the workflow graph in a half-applied state under concurrent cron or edits.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — `immediateDelete` cancels the provider batch and returns without deleting or marking the `WorkflowReminder`, so workflow/step deletion and rescheduling leave scheduled email rows orphaned indefinitely because the cron cleanup only selects `cancelled: true` rows.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:452 — the successful-payment rejection branch returns at line 464 before the new workflow-reminder cancellation loop, so cancelling a paid booking can still deliver its scheduled email/SMS reminders.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:486 — reminder cancellation calls are launched inside `forEach` but omitted from the awaited `Promise.all` at line 497, allowing the cancellation endpoint to finish before provider cancellation/database marking completes and leaving reminders active on serverless termination.

packages/prisma/migrations/20230217230604_add_cancelled_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql:2 — Adding `cancelled` as nullable without a default or backfill leaves every existing and newly created active reminder as NULL, so any active-state query using `cancelled = false` silently omits those rows and the lifecycle state cannot be migrated or reprocessed deterministically.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:80 — The `unscheduledReminders` query filters only `method`, `scheduled`, and `scheduledDate` and omits `cancelled: false`, so a cancelled reminder that is still unscheduled can be sent by the cron backfill before the cancellation cleanup reaches it.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:488 — `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId);` (and the SMS call on line 490) is launched from `forEach` without being collected or awaited, so the handler can send cancellation emails and return success before the reminder database/API cancellation finishes.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` invokes async cancellation functions without awaiting them, while the surrounding `try/catch` only observes synchronous errors, so `eventManager.reschedule(...)` can proceed before old reminders are cancelled and async failures escape the catch.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488 — `bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach(...)` starts async reminder cancellation without awaiting it, so the reschedule mutation can continue and complete while cancellation is still in flight.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:214 — `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true);` and the SMS equivalent are not awaited before `workflow.deleteMany(...)`, so deleting a workflow can return while remote scheduled-send cancellation is still pending.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:378 — `remindersToDelete.flat().forEach(...)` launches async cancellation calls and then immediately awaits only the event-type database updates, allowing new reminder scheduling to race with cancellation of the old reminders.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:576 — `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... })` is not awaited, so edited-step processing can create replacement reminders and return before the prior reminder cancellation/deletion completes.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:225 — `data: { cancelled: true }` only marks the reminder locally, while scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-50 polls cancelled reminders only through one hour before scheduledDate, so a cancellation made earlier than that leaves the already-scheduled SendGrid email active and it can still be delivered.

packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — The single `for` loop awaits each remote cancellation inside one outer try, so one SendGrid failure aborts the loop and leaves all later cancelled reminders neither cancelled remotely nor deleted locally while the handler continues.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:486 — `updatedBookings.forEach` invokes the async reminder cancellation functions without awaiting them and the subsequent `Promise.all` excludes those promises, so the endpoint can return success while SMS cancellation/DB deletion or email cancellation marking is still pending and a reminder can fire after cancellation.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:413 — The nested `steps.forEach(async ...)`, `bookingsForReminders.forEach(async ...)`, and `activeOn.forEach(async ...)` fan-out is never awaited, so the mutation can return before remote scheduling and relationship writes finish and any rejection becomes an unhandled partial update.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:505 — `userWorkflow.steps.map(async ...)` is discarded, so step deletion/update and its reminder cancellation can still be running after the mutation responds, with failures detached from the request and later edits racing the unfinished work.

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177 — `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` deletes the database row only after `twilio.cancelSMS` succeeds and swallows failures at line 187, while no SMS cancellation worker retries failed calls, leaving a provider-scheduled SMS live indefinitely after a transient cancellation error.

packages/features/ee/workflows/components/WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390 — The reminder-lifecycle task does not specify editor UI changes, yet this patch changes the SMS phone-verification render gate to `"{isPhoneNumberNeeded && ("`; that unrelated behavior can regress workflow-step configuration and is untraceable to the stated requirement.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — This newly added cancellation loop trusts the caller-supplied `rescheduleUid` booking lookup without an attendee/owner authorization check, so anyone who obtains another booking UID can cancel that booking's provider-backed email/SMS reminders (IDOR).

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that when cancelling reminders, the code sets `cancelled: true` on WorkflowReminder records (in emailReminderManager.ts lines 218-225). The cancellation cleanup in scheduleEmailReminders.ts (lines 43-73) only processes reminders where `cancelled: true` AND `scheduledDate` is within the next hour. However, looking at the unscheduledReminders query (which would be around line 80+ after the new code), it filters for `scheduled: false` but does not exclude `cancelled: true` reminders. This means a reminder that was marked as cancelled but hasn't been cleaned up yet (because its scheduledDate is more than an hour away) could still be picked up and sent by the unscheduled reminders processing logic. This is a valid race condition bug.

This means: 1) The code proceeds to eventManager.reschedule() before reminders are actually cancelled, 2) Any async errors from the cancellation functions will be unhandled Promise rejections that escape the catch block. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:225 — `data: { cancelled: true }` only marks the reminder locally, while scheduleEmailReminders.ts:43-50 polls cancelled reminders only through one hour before scheduledDate, so a cancellation made earlier than that leaves the already-scheduled SendGrid email active and it can still be delivered.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a timing gap in the cancellation logic. In emailReminderManager.ts, deleteScheduledEmailReminder marks reminders as cancelled=true in the database (lines 224-230). In scheduleEmailReminders.ts, the cron job only processes cancelled reminders where scheduledDate is within the next hour (lines 45-48: 'scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().add(1, "hour").toISOString() }'). If a booking is cancelled more than 1 hour before the scheduled reminder time, the reminder is marked cancelled but the cron job won't pick it up until within that 1-hour window. However, the SendGrid email was already scheduled with a batch_id when created. The cancellation in the cron job (lines 55-61) sends a cancel request to SendGrid, but if the email is scheduled to send before the cron runs (which runs periodically), the email could still be delivered. This is a real timing race condition bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:56 — The single `for` loop awaits each remote cancellation inside one outer try, so one SendGrid failure aborts the loop and leaves all later cancelled reminders neither cancelled remotely nor deleted locally while the handler continues.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a for loop (lines 54-70 in scheduleEmailReminders.ts) where each iteration awaits client.request() inside a single try-catch block. If any SendGrid API call fails, the catch block logs the error and the loop terminates, leaving subsequent reminders in the remindersToCancel array neither cancelled remotely nor deleted from the database. The workflowRemindersToDelete array would be incomplete, and Promise.all would only process the reminders that were successfully handled before the failure. This is a real bug where partial failure leaves the system in an inconsistent state.

The finding points to `userWorkflow.steps.map(async ...)` but the actual code shows `remindersFromStep.forEach((reminder) => {...})` and similar patterns where async operations like `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are called without awaiting. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177 — `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` deletes the database row only after `twilio.cancelSMS` succeeds and swallows failures at line 187, while no SMS cancellation worker retries failed calls, leaving a provider-scheduled SMS live indefinitely after a transient cancellation error.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows deleteScheduledSMSReminder at lines 177-189 in smsReminderManager.ts. The function calls twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId) first, then deletes the database record. If twilio.cancelSMS fails, the catch block at line 187 only logs the error and swallows it, meaning the database record won't be deleted but the SMS remains scheduled with Twilio. Unlike the email reminder manager which has a scheduled worker (scheduleEmailReminders.ts) that processes cancelled reminders, there's no equivalent retry mechanism for SMS shown in the diff. This means a transient Twilio API failure could leave an SMS scheduled indefinitely.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/components/WorkflowStepContainer.tsx:390 — The reminder-lifecycle task does not specify editor UI changes, yet this patch changes the SMS phone-verification render gate to `"{isPhoneNumberNeeded && ("`; that unrelated behavior can regress workflow-step configuration and is untraceable to the stated requirement.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the change from `(isPhoneNumberNeeded || isSenderIdNeeded)` to `isPhoneNumberNeeded` is 'unrelated' to the reminder-lifecycle task. However, looking at the diff, this is a UI simplification that removes the `isSenderIdNeeded` condition. The diff shows this is part of a larger refactoring effort. The finding incorrectly characterizes this as a regression risk when it's actually simplifying the conditional rendering logic.
